correctness.rationale: For every d>=2,N>=2 the quadrant indicator belongs to V1 tensor V1 and hence the sparse space. The retained longitudinal slice with transverse W1 is exactly V_(N-1), whose average of the negative jump is -1/2 on the adjacent odd cell. Both projected differences are exactly +1/4 there, so the Euler output is -(r_i+r_j)/4, strictly negative whenever at least one selected speed is positive. Extra coordinates differentiate constants to zero. Adding a smaller positive constant proves strict-input failure. At N=1 the positive cone is a>=sum|b_i| and each coefficient scales by 1-2r_i; this gives the exact iff bound. In d=1 the standard periodic full-grid upwind convex-combination criterion applies; N=0 is identity. Independent standard-library exact-rational projection code verified finite cases, not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The same natural low-order sparse-grid discretization known to achieve an enlarged sharp L2 CFL has no positivity-preserving positive Courant number at all once mixed level-one Haar functions enter, including for a single active velocity and strictly positive input. The complete dimension/level frontier gives a decisive algorithm-design boundary: reducing the time step or applying a generic positive CFL restriction cannot solve this specific issue; a change in spatial projection or nonlinear limiting is necessary. The exact one-quarter signed defect and low-level necessity/sufficiency make this substantially more informative than an arbitrary small negative numerical sample.
